log.text: Gholdengo used Make It Rain → Grimmsnarl

decisions.rationale: Lead Grimmsnarl Light Screen + Mega Gengar to pressure expected Blastoise+Gholdengo lead: Shadow Ball 2x and Shadow Tag trap Gholdengo, while screens blunt their special onslaught. Back Empoleon (Ice Beam vs Whimsicott, bulky Fairy/Ice resist) and Rotom-Mow (Thunderbolt vs the Water core) cover the back line. Avoid status on Gholdengo (Good as Gold).

Lead Whimsicott and Gholdengo to exploit priority disruption, threaten immediate spread damage, and deny Fake Out. Whimsicott can establish Tailwind or Taunt Trick Room/support, while Scarf Gholdengo pressures Gengar and Grimmsnarl. Mega Blastoise and Tauros provide strong midgame damage, Intimidate, and useful Water/Fighting coverage.
decisions.notebook: Opponent structure: Gengar may Mega Evolve for Shadow Tag and fast pressure; Grimmsnarl commonly uses Prankster Fake Out, Taunt, and Light Screen; Rotom-Mow threatens Water-types with Thunderbolt; Slowbro can set Trick Room. Gholdengo is immune to Fake Out and valuable against Grimmsnarl support. Preserve Mega Blastoise until Rotom-Mow is controlled or safe targets for Aura Sphere/Ice Beam appear. Whimsicott plus Gholdengo is a strong anti-support lead; retain Taunt for Trick Room or screens and Tailwind for speed control.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out (+3) flinches Whimsicott before its Prankster Taunt/Tailwind, neutralizing the screen-denier and speed-setter. Gengar Mega Evolves (~198 Speed, Shadow Tag traps Whimsicott) and Shadow Ball 2x into Gholdengo (66-148%, likely OHKO). Removing Gholdengo kills the Make It Rain threat and beats the Taunt-risk of screening; Grimmsnarl screens safely next turn.
decisions.notebook: Opponent can lead Whimsicott (Prankster, Focus Sash, Timid) + Gholdengo (Choice Scarf, Good as Gold, Modest) instead of Blastoise. Whimsicott Prankster Taunt denies Grimmsnarl screens (Whimsicott faster) -> Fake Out Whimsicott turn1 is the reliable counter (+3 priority flinch, denies Taunt/Tailwind). Gholdengo Choice Scarf speed 156-204; base Gengar 178 often outsped, but Mega Gengar (~198) usually outspeeds. Gengar Shadow Ball 2x OHKO-range vs Gholdengo (66-148% Mega). All foe attacks special -> Light Screen vital but only after Whimsicott neutralized. Shadow Tag traps non-Ghost foes (Whimsicott), not Ghost (Gholdengo, but Choice-locked anyway). Back mons likely Politoed (Drizzle/Icy Wind/Helping Hand) and/or Blastoise-Mega; beware mid-game rain + speed control. Avoid status on Gholdengo (Good as Gold immune).

decisions.rationale: Gengar-Mega stays (only Pass/Forfeit; forfeit loses). Switch Grimmsnarl->Empoleon: resists Whimsicott Moonblast (8-19% vs 24-58% Rotom) and rain core Water/Ice (Blastoise Ice Beam 3.7-8.2% vs Rotom 48-104% OHKO risk). Empoleon Flash Cannon 2x into Fairy Whimsicott (81.7-98.6%, crit OHKO) combines with Gengar Shadow Ball to remove trapped foe. Rotom-Mow's 2x Ice weakness and weaker Whimsicott matchup make it inferior.
decisions.notebook: Opponent tends to lead Whimsicott (Prankster, Focus Sash, Timid) + Gholdengo (Choice Scarf, Good as Gold, Modest). Whimsicott Prankster Taunt outspeeds Grimmsnarl screens; Fake Out (+3) flinch counters it. Mega Gengar (~200) outspeeds Scarf Gholdengo; Shadow Ball 2x OHKO-range. Shadow Tag traps non-Ghost (Whimsicott). Back mons likely Politoed (Drizzle) and/or Blastoise-Mega; beware rain + speed control. Avoid status on Gholdengo (Good as Gold). Empoleon resists Fairy/Ice/Water, strong vs Whimsicott (Flash Cannon 2x Fairy).

decisions.rationale: Taunt Grimmsnarl before it can establish Light Screen or other support, while Gholdengo uses spread Make It Rain to pressure both foes and heavily punish Grimmsnarl. Gholdengo is immune to Fake Out, and Tailwind is less urgent while its Choice Scarf already gives it excellent Speed.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Mega Blastoise for safer Water Spout/Aura Sphere/Ice Beam opportunities, especially after Rotom-Mow is controlled. Gholdengo remains valuable against Grimmsnarl support and Fake Out. Keep Whimsicott’s Taunt available for Trick Room, screens, or disruptive support; use Tailwind when opposing speed control or faster threats make it necessary.

decisions.rationale: Switch Tauros in to preserve Mega Blastoise while maintaining immediate pressure on the weakened Mega Gengar; Whimsicott can still threaten it with Moonblast or establish speed control.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Mega Blastoise for high-value Water Spout, Aura Sphere, or Ice Beam opportunities, especially once Rotom-Mow is controlled. Tauros-Paldea-Aqua provides useful Intimidate and immediate physical pressure. Keep Whimsicott’s Taunt available for Trick Room, screens, and disruptive support.

decisions.rationale: Gengar Protect (+4) outranks Whimsicott Prankster Taunt (+1), so it resolves first and safely blocks Tauros Aqua Jet; Gengar is also immune to Close Combat (Fighting vs Ghost 0x), guaranteeing survival this turn. Empoleon Flash Cannon (2x Steel) is a confirmed KO on Whimsicott (140-271%). Removing the Prankster support while keeping my Mega alive is the strongest line.
decisions.notebook: Opponent tends to lead Whimsicott (Prankster, Focus Sash, Timid) + Gholdengo (Choice Scarf, Good as Gold, Modest). Whimsicott Prankster Taunt; Fake Out (+3) flinch counters screens. Mega Gengar (~200) outspeeds Scarf Gholdengo; Shadow Ball 2x OHKO. Shadow Tag traps non-Ghost (Whimsicott). Back mons likely Politoed (Drizzle) / Blastoise-Mega; beware rain + speed control. Avoid status on Gholdengo (Good as Gold). Empoleon resists Fairy/Ice/Water; Flash Cannon 2x Whimsicott. Gengar immune to Fighting (Close Combat), so safe vs Tauros-Paldea-Aqua except Aqua Jet (priority, ~22-33%, not a guaranteed KO). Tauros-Paldea-Aqua: Intimidate + Aqua Jet (priority) + Close Combat (2x Empoleon). Protect (+4) beats Prankster Taunt (+1).

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Prankster Taunt shuts down Mega Gengar’s Psychic and Protect options, preventing its likely KO on Tauros. Tauros then applies immediate super-effective Close Combat pressure to Empoleon, with a possible OHKO; this also avoids wasting Tailwind while the faster threat remains uncontrolled.
decisions.notebook: Mega Blastoise remains the preferred preservation target for high-value Water Spout, Aura Sphere, or Ice Beam turns, especially after Rotom-Mow is controlled. Tauros-Paldea-Aqua is valuable for Intimidate and immediate physical pressure. Whimsicott’s Prankster Taunt should be prioritized against Trick Room, screens, Protect loops, and dangerous disruptive attackers. Monitor Empoleon’s Competitive before using further Intimidate.

decisions.rationale: Both target Tauros: Psychic (2x SE) + Thunderbolt (2x SE) combine for 133-318%, guaranteeing its removal. Gengar at 23% likely survives Tauros Aqua Jet (19.7-35.8%, ~77% survive at 4HP). Whimsicott has Focus Sash and resists Electric, so not worth targeting. Killing Tauros removes the Aqua Jet/Intimidate threat.
decisions.notebook: Opponent tends to lead Whimsicott (Prankster, Focus Sash, Timid) + Gholdengo (Choice Scarf, Good as Gold, Modest). Whimsicott: Taunt/Tailwind/Encore/Moonblast; Focus Sash blocks one KO. Gholdengo immune to status (Good as Gold) - avoid status; Scarf outspeeds most but Mega Gengar (~200) beats it; Shadow Ball 2x OHKO. Tauros-Paldea-Aqua: Intimidate, Aqua Jet (priority +1, ~20-36% into Gengar), Close Combat (Gengar immune), BlackBelt. Back mons likely Politoed (Drizzle) / Blastoise-Mega / Maushold (Follow Me). Gengar immune to Fighting; Shadow Tag traps non-Ghost. Mega Gengar frail (~23% here) - avoid leaving it exposed to priority.

decisions.rationale: Encore locks Gengar-Mega into its previously used Protect, while Tauros uses priority Aqua Jet to pressure its 23% HP and potentially KO. Whimsicott’s Prankster Encore resolves before Aqua Jet; if Protect blocks the hit, Gengar remains constrained and should lose its next protection cycle.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Mega Blastoise for high-value Water Spout, Aura Sphere, or Ice Beam turns, especially once Rotom-Mow is controlled. Tauros remains valuable for Intimidate and immediate physical pressure. Prioritize Whimsicott’s Prankster Taunt/Encore against Trick Room, screens, Protect loops, and disruptive attackers. Monitor Competitive before using Intimidate.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Gengar is Encore-locked to Protect (3rd use, ~1/3 success). Rotom Thunderbolt on Blastoise: 2x SE, 100% acc, reliable OHKO vs its speed-focused Modest build (near-0 SpD), eliminating opponent's only real threat besides Whimsicott. Preserves Rotom SpA for cleanup. If Gengar's Protect fails, Moonblast (0.5x) may KO at 23% but acceptable risk; winning requires removing Blastoise now.
decisions.notebook: Opponent series pattern: leads Whimsicott (Prankster, Focus Sash, Timid; Taunt/Tailwind/Encore/Moonblast) + Gholdengo (Choice Scarf, Good as Gold, Modest; Make It Rain/Shadow Ball/Thunderbolt/Trick). Gholdengo immune to status - never waste status; Mega Gengar (Spd 200) outspeeds Scarf and 2x Shadow Ball OHKOs. Tauros-Paldea-Aqua: Intimidate, BlackBelt, Aqua Jet priority, Close Combat (Gengar immune). Back line this series: Blastoise (Blastoisinite, Modest, speed-invested 98-130, not bulky; Ice Beam 2x on Rotom, Aura Sphere pulse under Mega Launcher but 0x vs Gengar), Maushold (Follow Me, not brought G2), Politoed (Drizzle, not brought G2). Gengar immune to Fighting; Shadow Tag traps non-Ghost. Mega Gengar frail (~23% after one hit) - avoid exposure to priority. Plan: remove Blastoise first (Thunderbolt 2x OHKO), then clean Whimsicott (Focus Sash intact, 0.5x Thunderbolt needs 2 hits).

decisions.rationale: Prankster Taunt shuts down Rotom-Mow before it can threaten Blastoise, while Gengar is locked into Encore-affected Protect. Blastoise then targets Rotom with super-effective Ice Beam without spending Mega Evolution on a non-boosted move, preserving Mega Blastoise for a stronger Water Spout or Aura Sphere turn.
decisions.notebook: Mega Blastoise should generally be preserved for high-value Water Spout, Aura Sphere, or Ice Beam turns where its power or survivability materially changes the position. Whimsicott’s Prankster Taunt and Encore are key tools for stopping Trick Room, screens, Protect loops, and disruptive attackers. Monitor Competitive before using Intimidate.

decisions.rationale: Gengar is Encore-locked into Protect (only legal move); must Protect since Whimsicott's Moonblast reaches up to 26.7% and Gengar sits at 23%. Rotom is Taunted, so only attacks are legal. Leaf Storm (38.9-74.8%) outchips Thunderbolt (26.3-51.9%) at equal 0.5x vs Whimsicott; Focus Sash is inactive at 85% HP. Whimsicott can't be KO'd this turn, but Encore ends next turn letting Gengar Shadow Ball (1x) finish it.
decisions.notebook: Opponent series pattern: leads Whimsicott (Prankster, Focus Sash, Timid; Taunt/Tailwind/Encore/Moonblast) + Gholdengo (Choice Scarf, Good as Gold, Modest; Make It Rain/Shadow Ball/Thunderbolt/Trick). Gholdengo immune to status - never waste status. Back line: Blastoise (Blastoisinite, Modest, speed 98-130; Ice Beam 2x on Rotom, Aura Sphere pulse 0x vs Gengar), Tauros-Paldea-Aqua (Intimidate, BlackBelt, Aqua Jet priority, Close Combat 0x vs Gengar), Maushold (Follow Me, not brought G2), Politoed (Drizzle, not brought G2). Mega Gengar (Spd 200) outspeeds Scarf Gholdengo; 2x Shadow Ball OHKOs Gholdengo. Rotom-Mow Thunderbolt 2x OHKOs Tauros and Blastoise. Whimsicott walls Rotom (Electric/Grass both 0.5x); needs Gengar Shadow Ball (1x) to finish. Gengar immune to Fighting; Shadow Tag traps non-Ghost. Mega Gengar frail - avoid priority exposure. Plan: remove Blastoise first, then chip Whimsicott with Rotom + free Gengar Shadow Ball.

decisions.rationale: Encore Rotom-Mow’s Taunt to prevent further status disruption while it is already Taunted, preserving Whimsicott’s control. Blastoise is fainted and must pass.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Mega Blastoise for decisive Water Spout, Aura Sphere, or Ice Beam turns when possible. Whimsicott control is central: use Prankster Taunt or Encore to stop Trick Room, screens, Protect loops, and disruptive moves. Monitor Competitive before using Intimidate.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott is the last foe at 43% HP (Focus Sash inactive, no Protect). Gengar Shadow Ball (1x, 47-93% of max) is a guaranteed KO and Gengar (Spd 200) outspeeds Whimsicott (max 184), striking first; Rotom Thunderbolt adds chip. This wins game 2.
decisions.notebook: Series best-of-3, currently 0-1 (must win G2 to force G3). Opponent leads Whimsicott (Prankster, Focus Sash, Timid; Taunt/Tailwind/Encore/Moonblast) + Gholdengo (Choice Scarf, Good as Gold, Modest; Make It Rain/Shadow Ball/Thunderbolt/Trick; status-immune). Back: Blastoise (Blastoisinite, Modest, spd 98-130; Ice Beam 2x on Rotom, Aura Sphere 0x vs Gengar), Tauros-Paldea-Aqua (Intimidate, BlackBelt, Aqua Jet priority, Close Combat 0x vs Gengar), Maushold (Follow Me, not brought G2), Politoed (Drizzle, not brought G2). Mega Gengar (Spd 200) outspeeds Scarf Gholdengo; 2x Shadow Ball OHKOs Gholdengo. Rotom Thunderbolt 2x OHKOs Tauros/Blastoise. Whimsicott walls Rotom (Elec/Grass 0.5x); needs Gengar Shadow Ball (1x). Gengar immune to Fighting; Shadow Tag traps non-Ghost. Mega Gengar frail - avoid priority exposure.

decisions.rationale: Encore Gengar to force another Protect attempt and preserve control while Rotom remains locked into Thunderbolt by Encore. This denies Gengar a damaging or disruptive move and creates the best chance to stabilize and exploit the remaining turns.
decisions.notebook: Whimsicott control remains the central win condition. Preserve Mega Blastoise for a decisive Water Spout, Aura Sphere, or Ice Beam turn whenever possible. Avoid Intimidate against teams with Competitive unless the payoff is decisive.

decisions.rationale: Both are Encore-locked: Gengar must Protect (blocks Whimsicott's Moonblast), Rotom must Thunderbolt. Whimsicott is at 4% (Focus Sash inactive, not full HP) and trapped by Shadow Tag, so Thunderbolt guarantees the KO. Opponent has no other active or brought Pokémon, so this wins game 2 and forces game 3.
decisions.notebook: Series 0-1, must win G2 to force G3. Opponent team: Whimsicott (Prankster, Focus Sash, Timid; Taunt/Tailwind/Encore/Moonblast), Gholdengo (Choice Scarf, Good as Gold, Modest; Make It Rain/Shadow Ball/Thunderbolt/Trick), Blastoise (Blastoisinite, Modest; Ice Beam/Aura Sphere/Water Spout/Protect), Tauros-Paldea-Aqua (Intimidate, BlackBelt; Aqua Jet/Close Combat/Raging Bull/Protect), Maushold (Follow Me, not brought G2), Politoed (Drizzle, not brought G2). Mega Gengar (Spd 200) outspeeds Scarf Gholdengo; 2x Shadow Ball OHKOs Gholdengo. Rotom Thunderbolt 2x OHKOs Tauros/Blastoise. Whimsicott walls Rotom (0.5x); needs Gengar Shadow Ball. Gengar immune to Fighting; Shadow Tag traps non-Ghost. Mega Gengar frail - avoid priority exposure.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott cannot survive Rotom-Mow’s encored Thunderbolt, and Moonblast cannot KO Rotom from 62% (estimated maximum damage is below its remaining HP). This is the only non-concession action that can deal meaningful damage before the loss.
decisions.notebook: Whimsicott remains the key control piece; preserve it when possible and use Encore/Taunt sequencing to deny opposing Protect or setup. Mega Blastoise should be reserved for a decisive Water Spout, Aura Sphere, or Ice Beam turn. Avoid Intimidate into Competitive unless the payoff is decisive.

reflections.summary: Won because lead Mega Gengar + Grimmsnarl disrupted opponent: Gengar Shadow Ball OHKOed Scarf Gholdengo and Grimmsnarl Fake Out flinched Whimsicott, then Rotom-Mow Thunderbolt cleaned Tauros/Blastoise. The four brought (Mega Gengar, Grimmsnarl, Empoleon, Rotom-Mow) and evolving Gengar were well-suited to opponent's Ghost/Electric weaknesses.
reflections.adjustment: Avoid repeated Gengar Protect (PP failed, left it Encore-locked by Whimsicott); use Gengar Taunt on Whimsicott early to negate Encore/Taunt and consider a Whimsicott-specific attacker for game 3.
reflections.notebook: Series tied 1-1. Opponent G2 lead: Whimsicott+Gholdengo; brought Tauros-Aqua, Blastoise; Maushold/Politoed unused. Mega Gengar outspeeds/OHKOs Gholdengo; Rotom Thunderbolt 2x vs Tauros/Blastoise. Whimsicott resists Electric (Grass) and uses Encore/Taunt to lock Gengar Protect (PP depletion caused fail). Grimmsnarl Fake Out effective. G3 plan: keep Mega Gengar; Taunt Whimsicott early; manage Protect PP; expect possible Maushold Follow Me or Politoed Drizzle if opponent adjusts.

reflections.summary: Lost primarily because the brought four and Mega Blastoise plan were poorly suited to the opponent: Gholdengo and Tauros were traded away early, while Rotom-Mow immediately removed Mega Blastoise and then outlasted Whimsicott. The repeated Protect cycle also made the remaining control plan unable to create damage.
reflections.adjustment: Reconsider the preview lineup by replacing Mega Blastoise with Garchomp and preserve Whimsicott alongside a direct offensive threat; do not commit Blastoise into this Rotom-Mow matchup. Use Taunt or Encore to force Gengar or Rotom off Protect, then attack the exposed target rather than allowing repeated protection.
reflections.notebook: Gengar-Mega and Rotom-Mow both relied heavily on Protect; Encore and Taunt can constrain them, but damage must be timed during the forced turns. Rotom-Mow carries strong single-target Electric pressure and can punish Tauros and Mega Blastoise, so avoid centering the four around Blastoise. Grimmsnarl used early Fake Out support, while Empoleon's Competitive makes Intimidate an unfavorable default unless the payoff is decisive. Preserve Whimsicott when possible and pair its control with immediate pressure.
